claim: Laredo's Puebla Vieja is a medieval Historic-Artistic Site of rúas with noble mansions, all leading to the Gothic Iglesia de Santa María de la Asunción, which holds the Flemish-style Bethlehem altarpiece.
quote: The heart of the original settlement is the medieval Puebla Vieja, declared a Historic-Artistic Site... All the streets lead to Iglesia de Santa María de la Asunción, a Gothic-style church that is home to the Virgin of Bethlehem altarpiece, one of the most important Flemish-style pieces in the country.

claim: Laredo's Playa Salvé is the longest beach in Cantabria at over 4,250 metres, sheltered by Monte Buciero into calm, family-friendly waters.
quote: Playa Salvé is the longest beach in Cantabria, stretching over 4,250 metres, located at the end of the Asón River estuary within a bay protected by Monte Buciero, creating calm and safe waters with fine, white, and golden sand ideal for family enjoyment.

claim: Laredo's Puebla Vieja was declared a historic-artistic site in 1970 and still preserves remains of its ancient walls; the town also has a fishing port and a sports marina with 850+ moorings.
quote: Puebla Vieja and its Arrabal, declared a historic artistic site in 1970, which is the primitive population nucleus with medieval origins and still preserves remains of its ancient walls... the modern Sports Port of Laredo, a modern installation with more than 850 moorings

claim: Laredo's Battle of Flowers (Batalla de Flores), held the last Friday of August, is a parade of flower-decorated floats and is declared of national tourist interest.
quote: The "Batalla de Flores" (Battle of Flowers) festival, celebrated the last Friday of August, which is of national tourist interest

claim: Santoña, the anchovy capital, offers gastronomic tours of anchovy workshops plus the Santoña Marshes Natural Reserve at the mouth of the Asón River with waterfowl viewing year-round.
quote: Santoña is the Capital of the Anchoa... The Santoña Marshes Natural Reserve (at the mouth of the Asón River) is a protected area with great ecosystem variety that throughout the year allows seeing different species of waterfowl.

claim: Santoña preserves three defensive fortifications on Monte Buciero — Fort San Martín, Fort San Carlos and Fort del Mazo (Napoleón) — with views over the bay.
quote: Three defensive fortifications: Fort San Martín, Fort San Carlos, and Fort del Mazo (or "de Napoleón"), located on Buciero with magnificent views of the territory

claim: Santoña's Faro del Caballo is reached by 763 stairs originally built by Santoña prison inmates in the 19th century and rebuilt in 2013; the lighthouse operated 1863–1993.
quote: The most common way to reach the lighthouse is via more than 700 steps that were built by inmates of the Santoña prison in the nineteenth century. In 2013, the 763 stairs were rebuilt... The lighthouse began operating on August 31, 1863, and in 1993, after 130 years of service, it stopped

claim: The Faro del Caballo + Faro del Pescador trail from Santoña promenade is roughly 5 miles round-trip with ~500 m elevation gain and takes 3.5–4 hours — a hard hike with handrails and ropes on the steep descent.
quote: covers 5.2 miles with an elevation gain of 1,637 feet and takes about 3.5–4 hours to complete. Although the steps may seem dangerous at first glance, there are handrails and ropes installed that make the tour much safer.

claim: Liérganes, one of Los Pueblos Más Bonitos de España, has a 16th-century Renaissance Puente Mayor over the Miera river, a Hombre Pez statue and over 20 baroque/neoclassical buildings in a stone old town.
quote: Liérganes ostenta el título de uno de los Pueblos más Bonitos de España... su icónico Puente Mayor, que aunque lo llamen "puente romano", en realidad es una joya renacentista del siglo XVI que cruza el río Miera. Allí encontrarás la estatua del Hombre Pez

claim: Liérganes' Casa de los Cañones on the Plaza Marqués de Valdecilla is decorated with cannons recalling the town's 17th-century cannon-foundry history; an old mill by the bridge is now the Centro de Interpretación de la Leyenda del Hombre Pez.
quote: Casa de los Cañones, un edificio del siglo XVIII, sus esquinas aparecen adornadas con cañones en recuerdo a una de las facetas clave de la economía de Liérganes: la fabricación de armas. El molino aledaño al puente estuvo en funcionamiento entre los siglos XVII y XIX, para ahora pasar a ser el Centro de Interpretación de la Leyenda del Hombre Pez.

claim: Liérganes' Balneario, built in 1913 around the Fuente Santa mineral-medicinal springs (declared of public utility 1869), sits in a 3-hectare park and offers thermal pools and treatments.
quote: The Balneario de Liérganes is known for its mineral-medicinal waters that emerge from the Fuente Santa (Holy Spring). The waters were declared of Public Utility in 1869. The spa was built in 1913 and is surrounded by a splendid three-hectare park with century-old trees.

claim: Pedreña is the birthplace of Seve Ballesteros, who debuted as a caddie at Real Golf de Pedreña aged 9 (his father worked there as a gardener) and learned to play hitting balls on the beach with a discarded 3-iron.
quote: Seve Ballesteros was born in Pedreña and played almost all his early golf at the club at Real Golf de Pedreña. His father worked as a gardener in Pedreña golf club, where Severiano made his debut as a caddie at the age of 9.

claim: Real Golf de Pedreña is a Harry Colt design from 1928 on a wooded peninsula in the Bay of Santander, extended in 1991 with 9 new holes designed by Seve Ballesteros himself.
quote: Located on a small wooded peninsula jutting into the Bay of Santander, Real Pedrena is a Harry Colt design that dates back to 1928. The 18-hole course was designed by Harry S. Colt in 1929 and in 1991, the course was extended with nine new holes designed and built by Severiano Ballesteros.

claim: Pedreña has a Seve statue welcoming visitors at the village entrance plus a park featuring a faux-Swilcan Bridge and a bronze cast of Seve's iconic fist-pump from the 1984 Open Championship.
quote: A statue in his honor gives welcome to all who arrive at the village, and in a park in Pedreña there is a faux-Swilcan Bridge and bronze statue capturing Seve's iconic fist-pump that followed his victorious birdie on the 72nd final hole of the 1984 Open Championship.

claim: Santillana del Mar — borderline at ~40 km west via A-67 — is a traffic-free medieval town anchored by the 12th-century Romanesque Colegiata de Santa Juliana with celebrated carved cloister capitals, paired with the Altamira Museum's replica neocave (the original cave is closed).
quote: the Colegiata de Santa Juliana, then pair your day with Altamira Museum & Neocave nearby. The town itself is traffic free and its narrow streets are lined with beautiful medieval buildings.

claim: Santillana del Mar is celebrated as one of Spain's most beautiful medieval villages, known for the Colegiata de Santa Juliana, the Convent of the Poor Clares, and proximity to the UNESCO Altamira Cave.
